newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB offers to buy five pct of grower equity in WIF.
newsitem.headline: AWB offers to buy five pct of grower equity in WIF.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Tuesday it was offering to buy a guaranteed five percent of individual growers equity in the Wheat Industry Fund (WIF).
The buyback, similar to a dividend on a share investment, is substantially the same as in previous years, AWB said.
This is the fourth year the AWB has extended the offer.

WIF secretary Andrew Heard said the five percent would achieve a balance between a regular return for growers on their investment and the WIF target size of A$550 million by June 30 1999. Payments to growers who wish to sell more than the guarantee would depend on the number of applicants, he said.
The AWB has allocated A$17.6 million to fund the payments. Payment will be based on the value of units at March 31.
The WIF is funded by levies on growers and is designed to provide commercial backing for AWB loans when Australia's federal government guarantee on borrowings by the statutory authority end in 1999.
